abstract:
Regulator of G-protein signaling 13 (RGS13) plays a tumor suppressor role in a variety of cancers, but its expression, function, and regulatory mechanism in colorectal cancer (CRC) are still unclear.
RGS13 expression in CRC was verified by bioinformatics analysis (GEO, GEPIA, and TNMplot) and clinical samples (qRT-PCR and western blot). In vitro, the effects of RGS13 overexpression on CRC cell proliferation, angiogenesis, metastasis, and glycolysis were evaluated using colony formation, tube formation, Transwell, and wound healing assays, and a glycolysis detection kit. The effect of RGS13 on apoptosis of CD8+ T cells was analyzed by a co-culture system and flow cytometry. In vivo, the tumor suppressive effect of RGS13 was verified by a xenograft tumor model in nude mice. Bioinformatics prediction, dual-luciferase reporter assay, and the rescue experiment were used to explore the transcriptional regulation of FOXD3 on RGS13.
RGS13 was downregulated in CRC tissues and cells, and its low expression was associated with poor prognosis of patients with CRC. Overexpression of RGS13 significantly inhibited the proliferation, angiogenesis, invasion, migration, and glycolysis of CRC cells, as well as suppressed the apoptosis of CD8+ T cells in the co-culture system. In vivo experiments confirmed that RGS13 overexpression reduced the growth of transplanted CRC tumors. FOXD3 directly bound to the promoter region of RGS13 to activate its transcription. In addition, FOXD3 played a role in inhibiting the malignant progression of CRC and CD8+ T-cell apoptosis by upregulating RGS13.
The FOXD3/RGS13 axis not only directly inhibits the malignant behavior of CRC cells but also represses CD8+ T-cell apoptosis by regulating the tumor microenvironment.

summary: Wet-lab study showing FOXD3 transcriptionally activates tumor suppressor RGS13, which inhibits colorectal cancer cell malignancy and CD8+ T cell apoptosis.
title: FOXD3 promotes the transcription of RGS13 to inhibit colorectal cancer malignant progression and CD8+ T cell apoptosis.
